about: The single source of the word lists the engine-side guards read. scripts/gen-agency-lexicon.mjs writes them into the JavaScript, Python and Go engines between BEGIN and END GENERATED GUARD LEXICON markers, and its --check (run by test/agency-lexicon.test.mjs) fails when any engine's copy drifts. Two guards read them. The negator window: a negator (the agency lexicon's negators and localNegators), or any n't contraction, among the two words before a match, with no clauseBreaks character between them. Strip keeps an intensifier there, and absolute.universal leaves an absolute there unmarked (its window also ends at a comma once a word stands between them). The imperative 'Never': a clause-initial 'never' followed by a lowercase word reads as advice and is not marked by absolute.universal, unless that word, after any neverPassThrough adverbs, is one of neverNonVerbs. The engines compare a word after ASCII-only lowercasing (a negator also after trimming apostrophes), so every word here is lowercase ASCII.
localNegatorsWhy: The guards' negators are the agency lexicon's negators (spec/agency-lexicon.json) and these: one vocabulary, so 'Nothing extremely bad happened', 'Nobody was extremely hurt' and 'Nothing is guaranteed' keep what they deny, as 'No customer data was accessed' does. A negator negates the intensifier or absolute after it: deleting 'extremely' from 'not extremely high' leaves 'not high', a stronger claim than the source made, and 'not guaranteed' and 'hardly always' are disclaimers, not overclaims. These two negate only the word right after them, so they suit the guards' two-word window but not the agency detector's clause-wide reading, where 'Without warning, customer data was exposed' still hides who exposed it.
neverNonVerbsWhy: Words that, after a clause-initial 'never', open a fragment ('Never an issue.') or an inversion ('Never has a product been this good.'), both claims, and do not begin advice, so absolute.universal keeps 'Never' marked before them.
neverPassThroughWhy: Adverbs that may stand between 'Never' and its verb: the word after them decides. 'Never ever share it.' is advice; 'Never again will prices be this low.' is an inversion; 'Never again.' is a fragment.
neverAdviceOpenersWhy: Words that can begin advice after 'Never' as well as an inversion, so they are not neverNonVerbs: the advice stays unmarked and the claim goes unmarked with it. 'Never have regrets.' but 'Never have I seen...'; 'Never at any time disclose your PIN.' but 'Never in history has...'; 'Never so much as glance at it.'; 'Never should you share it.' The inversions are recorded misses, in the safe direction. The engines do not read this list; the tests and the differential probe each word as unmarked.
